blocks.content: Aspose.Slides for Python via .NET (foss) now supports threaded comments with authors, timestamps, and positions — enabling collaborative review workflows directly within PowerPoint presentations. This feature allows teams to track feedback, assign responsibilities, and maintain context across slide revisions without external tools.

Developers can integrate rich comment threading into their slide automation workflows, preserving authorship and timing information for auditability and collaboration. Combined with the library’s existing support for slide manipulation, image handling, and shape creation, this enhancement strengthens Aspose.Slides as a production-grade solution for Python-based presentation automation.

import aspose_slides_foss as slides
from aspose_slides_foss import SaveFormat

with slides.Presentation() as prs:
    slide = prs.slides[0]  # first slide exists by default
    prs.save("new.pptx", SaveFormat.PPTX)

Aspose.Slides for Python now supports threaded comments with full authorship, timestamp, and positioning metadata—ideal for collaborative review workflows in slide decks. This feature enables developers to programmatically add structured feedback directly to slides, preserving context and timeline for team reviews.

blocks.content:
from datetime import datetime
import aspose_slides_foss as slides
from aspose_slides_foss import PointF

with slides.Presentation() as prs:
    author = prs.comment_authors.add_author("Jane Smith", "JS")
    slide = prs.slides[0]
    author.comments.add_comment("Review this slide", slide, PointF(2.0, 2.0), datetime.now())
    prs.save("comments.pptx", slides.SaveFormat.PPTX)

Aspose.Slides for Python via .NET (foss) enables threaded comments with authors, timestamps, and precise positions. This feature supports collaborative review workflows in presentation documents. To get started, install the library and use the `aspose_slides_foss` package to load, modify, and save PowerPoint files with full fidelity.

import aspose_slides_foss as slides
from aspose_slides_foss import SaveFormat

with slides.Presentation() as prs:
    prs.document_properties.title = "Q1 Results"
    prs.document_properties.author = "Finance Team"
    prs.document_properties.set_custom_property_value("Version", 3)
    prs.save("deck.pptx", SaveFormat.PPTX)
